Pakistan vs Vietnam for Clothing Manufacturing: Honest 2026 Comparison

✎ FABRIOZA Team 📅 July 26, 2026 🔄 Updated: July 26, 2026 ☕ 8 min read
Home › Blog › Pakistan vs Vietnam
TL;DR: Vietnam leads on technical outerwear, footwear-adjacent products and FTA-driven duty savings (CPTPP, EVFTA) — but labor costs roughly double Pakistan's and MOQs of 500–1,000+ shut out small brands. Pakistan offers 50-piece MOQs, stronger knits/sportswear/fleece capability and lower prices on cotton-based garments. Startups and sports/street brands: Pakistan. Large technical outerwear programs: Vietnam.

Vietnam has become the poster child of "China plus one" sourcing, and for good reason — but it is optimized for a very different customer than a growing independent brand. Here is where each country actually wins in 2026.

Quick Comparison Table

Where Vietnam Wins

Vietnam's factories serve the world's largest sportswear labels, and it shows in technical capability: laminated shells, taped seams, complex synthetic constructions and factory-floor discipline are world class. Its trade-agreement network (CPTPP, the EU–Vietnam FTA) progressively removes duties into major markets, which matters enormously at container scale. If you are placing a 20,000-piece technical jacket program, Vietnam belongs on your shortlist.

Where Pakistan Wins

  • Access for smaller brands. Vietnamese factories fed by tier-1 sportswear programs rarely accept sub-1,000-piece orders. Pakistan's industry routinely runs 50-piece styles — and FABRIOZA accepts 20-piece trial orders.
  • Cotton economics. Vietnam imports most fabric (largely from China), adding cost and lead time. Pakistan grows cotton and knits/dyes it domestically — a structural price advantage on tees, fleece hoodies and jersey products.
  • Decorated sportswear. Sublimated team kits, embroidered hoodies and puff-print streetwear are Sialkot specialties with local decoration supply chains — see our sportswear range.
  • Labor cost. Rising Vietnamese wages (roughly double Pakistan's) keep pushing cost-sensitive cut-and-sew work elsewhere.

Duties: Check Your Import Country

For EU brands, both countries can enter at 0%% (Vietnam via EVFTA phase-downs, Pakistan via GSP+ — verify current status). For the US, neither has an FTA, so standard MFN rates apply to both and the FOB price difference decides. For the UK, Pakistan's DCTS preference is a genuine cost edge.

The Decision Rule

Technical outerwear at volume: Vietnam. Cotton-based, decorated, or small-batch apparel: Pakistan. If you are under 1,000 pieces per style, Vietnamese factories will mostly not quote you seriously — start with a Pakistani factory and scale. Also see: Pakistan vs China and Pakistan vs Bangladesh.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Vietnam or Pakistan cheaper for clothing manufacturing?

Pakistan is generally cheaper on cotton-based garments (tees, hoodies, fleece) thanks to home-grown cotton and labor costs roughly half of Vietnam's. Vietnam can win on synthetic technical garments at large volume where its FTA duty savings kick in.

Why do small brands struggle to manufacture in Vietnam?

Vietnam's export factories are structured around large programs for global labels, so MOQs of 500-1,000+ pieces per style are standard and small RFQs are often ignored. Pakistan's low-MOQ culture (50 pieces, trial orders from 20) is far more accessible.

Which country is better for activewear and gym wear?

Both are credible. Vietnam dominates tier-1 technical activewear at volume; Pakistan offers seamless and sublimated activewear at 50-set MOQs with much lower entry cost - better for independent brands.

Does Vietnam have better quality than Pakistan?

At the top end both produce excellent quality. Vietnam's average is pulled up by tier-1 sportswear programs; in Pakistan, quality tracks the individual factory - choose ISO 9001-certified, socially audited factories and inspect samples.

What lead times should I expect from Vietnam vs Pakistan?

Vietnam: typically 45-90 days including fabric import from China. Pakistan: 2-4 weeks for small orders using local fabric, plus 3-7 days express shipping.
